name.title: From a quiet mind, a new language grows.
name.body: Zenzu grows from Zen: calm, presence, inner quiet. Fluency doesn't come from frantic streaks, but from a steady, unhurried mind. Speaking another language should feel like walking into a forest: you breathe, you slow down, and every word takes root like a tree in your grove.

features.title: Everything you need to learn
features.subtitle: One app for all your language learning content. Import what you love, learn what matters.

lisa.title: Lisa, Your AI Coach
lisa.desc: Ask Lisa for study plans, word explanations, or daily reviews. She replies in your language: English, Ukrainian, German, Spanish, French, or Portuguese.

more.what: Ask Lisa what a word means, why a sentence is built the way it is, or what to study today. You can also talk with her about a topic you choose. After the talk, you see your mistakes with the correct forms.
more.how: Before she answers, Lisa looks at your level, your progress, your due cards and your decks. When you ask her to save words or create a deck, she shows a proposal, and nothing changes until you confirm it. Between sessions she keeps short notes about you; you can read and delete them in Settings.
more.note: Lisa replies in your interface language: English, Ukrainian, German, Spanish, French or Portuguese. If you ask, she changes to another language.

youtube.title: YouTube Videos
youtube.desc: Watch with a live transcript. Tap a word or select a phrase, and Zenzu saves it as a card with full sentence context and native pronunciation.

more.what: Watch a YouTube video with its transcript under the player. The line being spoken is highlighted, and the transcript scrolls to keep it in view. Tap a word to see its translation, then save the word, a phrase or the whole sentence as a card.
more.how: Zenzu loads a transcript of the video in the language you learn, usually the captions the video already has. Each card keeps the sentence it came from and its translation, and “Open at source” takes you back to that moment in the video. You can repeat one sentence in a loop and change the playback speed.
more.note: To tap and save words, you need a transcript in the language you learn; when Zenzu cannot load one, no transcript is shown, only a message that no subtitles were found. Videos whose owner has turned off playback on other sites cannot play in Zenzu.

podcasts.title: Podcasts
podcasts.desc: AI-transcribed episodes you can read while you listen. Select any phrase to capture it as a card with pronunciation on every word.

more.what: Read the transcript of an episode while you listen. Tap a word, a phrase or a sentence to see the translation and save it as a card.
more.how: Find a show in the Apple Podcasts directory and subscribe; new episodes come from the show's feed. Zenzu transcribes an episode with speech recognition: each word gets a time stamp, and the spoken language is detected automatically.
more.note: Episodes longer than three hours are not transcribed.

starterDecks.title: Starter Decks
starterDecks.desc: 18 hand-curated decks from A1 to C1: everyday essentials, business, academic, science, idioms, and more. Deck names adapt to your interface language.

more.what: Start with ready decks of everyday words and phrases, from A1 to C1: food, travel, work, feelings, idioms, business and science. Every card has an example sentence, so you see the word in context from the first review.
more.how: In most decks, each card exists in nine languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese. The front is in the language you learn and the back is in your native language; if your native language is not on this list, the backs are translated when you add the deck. You can filter the catalog by language and level.
more.note: Some decks are made for particular languages, such as the irregular-verb tables or the false-friend decks for English and German; their cards come in fewer languages. Deck names show in your interface language.

interface.title: Interface in 6 Languages
interface.desc: Use the app in English, Ukrainian, German, Spanish, French, or Portuguese. Learn from your native tongue, not through English.

more.what: Menus, hints and Lisa's replies appear in your language: English, Ukrainian, German, Spanish, French or Portuguese. Card translations go into your native language, so you learn without English in between.
more.how: By default, the app follows the native language in your profile. You can also follow the language of your device or choose one in Settings.
more.note: You can learn English, German, French or Spanish. If the interface does not exist in your native language, for example Italian or Polish, translations still go into it, and the app shows another interface language.

courses.title: AI Courses
courses.desc: Personalized grammar and vocabulary lessons for English, German, French, and Spanish, from A1 to C1. Exercises adapt to your level.

more.what: Work through grammar and vocabulary lessons for English, German, French or Spanish, level by level from A1, up to C1 where the lessons are ready. A lesson appears only when a version for your language is ready; the German, French and Spanish courses also use the English version. So for now some language pairs have only part of the lessons, or none yet. Words from a lesson can go into your decks for review.
more.how: A lesson has stages such as new words, grammar, a dialogue and a recap, each with exercises: multiple choice, gap fill, matching, sentence building and dictation. Later lessons bring back earlier words with their translation. A short placement test sets your level; all levels up to it are open, and without the test you start at A1.
more.note: In the German, French and Spanish courses, explanations come in English when your language has no version. Lessons are prepared in advance; they are not generated for each learner.

srs.title: FSRS-6 Spaced Repetition
srs.desc: Science-backed algorithm schedules reviews at the optimal time. Remember words forever.

more.what: Each day you see the cards that are due, not the whole deck. Cards you know well come back less often, and cards you forget come back sooner.
more.how: After each card you rate how well you recalled it: Again, Hard, Good or Easy. FSRS-6 keeps a stability value and a difficulty value for each card and sets the next review date from them; each button shows the interval it will give. Recognition (word to meaning) and production (meaning to word) have separate schedules.
more.note: The schedule aims to show a card when your chance of recalling it drops to about 90%. Zenzu uses the default parameters of the open-source FSRS-6 algorithm.

tts.title: Native Pronunciation
tts.desc: Cloud TTS for every word and sentence. Hear how it sounds from day one.

more.what: Play any word or sentence in the language you learn with a cloud voice. In lesson dialogues, each word is highlighted as it is spoken.
more.how: Zenzu creates the audio on the server and caches it; the audio of a card loads when the card appears. You set the listening speed, and the same clip plays at that speed.
more.note: The voices are synthetic, not recordings of native speakers. When cloud audio is off or not available, the app uses the voice of your device.

import.title: Import from Anywhere
import.desc: Text, photos, articles: paste or snap anything. AI extracts vocabulary matched to your level.

more.what: Paste a text or a link to an article, or take up to four photos of one page: a book, a menu, a sign or handwritten notes. Zenzu finds words that match the level of the deck you import into and shows them as a list. You choose which ones become cards.
more.how: Each word comes with the sentence it stood in, copied from the source, and a translation of that sentence into your native language; when the source has no full sentence, such as a menu or a sign, Zenzu writes a short example instead. Each word is marked with its level; at first the list shows only the deck's level and higher, and you can add the lower levels. If the deck has no single level, Zenzu picks intermediate and advanced words and shows every level.
more.note: If you learn several languages, the text itself decides which language the words belong to. On iOS, you can share text and links from other apps to the Zenzu inbox and import them later.

forWhom.title: For those who take language seriously
forWhom.subtitle: Zenzu is a serious tool, not a toy. No cute mascots, no game to win. It's for people who want to own their progress and their data. Learning a language is one of the most demanding, most rewarding things you can do. Zenzu is built for that.
forWhom.for1: You believe real fluency comes from engaging with authentic content
forWhom.for2: You're committed to daily review, even on hard days
forWhom.for3: You have ambitious goals: reading a novel, working, or living in another language
forWhom.for4: You want tools that respect your memory, not just your screen time
forWhom.for5: You want your words, cards and progress to stay yours and reachable from your own AI agents through MCP
forWhom.notFor1: You're looking for a game with streaks and virtual trophies
forWhom.notFor2: You expect to speak fluently after a few casual sessions
forWhom.notFor3: You need gamification to stay motivated

mcp.title: Your data, wherever you work.
mcp.intro: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets an AI assistant use tools from other apps. Zenzu has its own MCP server. Connect Claude, Cursor or another assistant that supports MCP, and it can read your decks, cards and progress. If you allow it, it can also add, edit and delete cards and record your reviews.

scenarios.deck: Paste a text or an article. The assistant picks the most useful words for your level and saves them as cards in a deck.
scenarios.review: Review your due cards in the chat. The assistant asks one card at a time and records each answer with the same FSRS-6 scheduler as the app.
scenarios.confused: Find the words you mix up. The assistant sees which cards you confuse with each other and which ones you keep forgetting.
scenarios.report: Get a weekly report: reviews, active days, trouble words, your place in the course and one thing to focus on next week.
scenarios.media: Find a ready-made word deck for a film or a TV series and look through its cards.
scenarios.level: Ask where you stand: your level, your place in the course and the next lesson.

steps: In the app, open Settings → AI agents and choose Generate. Give the token a name, then copy it: the app shows it only once.
In your assistant, add Zenzu as an MCP server with the server URL from the same screen and your token.
Ask in plain words. The assistant picks the Zenzu tools it needs.
safety: Give each assistant its own personal token, with a name you choose.
A token can only read, unless you tick “Allow writes” when you create it. Writing lets the assistant create, edit and delete decks and cards, move cards, record reviews and write notebooks.
Revoke a token at any time on the same screen. It stops working at once.
You can have up to 10 active tokens.
An assistant sees only your account. It cannot reach other people's data.

meta.title: Zenzu MCP server: setup, tools and rules
meta.description: Connect your Zenzu decks and progress to Claude, Cursor or another assistant that supports remote MCP with a bearer token. Setup, tools, rules.

mcpPage.title: Zenzu MCP server
mcpPage.lead: Zenzu runs a hosted MCP server, so there is nothing to install. Your assistant connects to one URL over Streamable HTTP and signs in with a personal token from the app. This page shows the setup, every tool, the ready-made prompts and the rules the server keeps.

setup.generic: Create a token in the app: Settings → AI agents → Generate. Copy it at once: the app shows it only once. In your client, add a remote MCP server with this URL and send the token in the Authorization header. Replace zmcp_… with your token.
setup.claudeCode: Run this command in a terminal, with your token in place of zmcp_…. By default Claude Code adds the server to the current project only. Add --scope user to use it in all your projects.

mcpPage.toolsIntro: You ask in plain words, and your assistant picks the tools it needs. Tools that change your data work only with a token that has “Allow writes”.

tools.list_decks: Your decks, with card counts and the number of cards due now.
tools.get_deck_cards: The cards of one deck, soonest due first. Up to 50 per call.
tools.search_my_cards: Searches all your cards by front, back and context sentence. Up to 30 results per call.
tools.update_deck: Renames a deck or changes its description, language or label colour.
tools.delete_deck: Deletes a deck and all its cards. This cannot be undone.
tools.add_card: Adds one card to a deck as a new card.
tools.add_cards: Adds up to 50 cards to a deck in one call.
tools.update_card: Edits the text of a card. Its review schedule does not change.
tools.delete_card: Moves a card to the trash. It is deleted for good after 30 days.
tools.move_card: Moves a card to another deck. Its review schedule does not change.
tools.list_inbox_items: Texts, links and YouTube videos in your inbox that you have not imported yet.
tools.get_due_cards: The cards due now, in the same order as a review session in the app. New cards are not included.
tools.review_card: Records your answer to a card (again, hard, good or easy) with the same FSRS-6 scheduler as the app.
tools.get_review_history: Your recent reviews: which card, which rating and when. Up to 100 rows.
tools.get_interference_pairs: Pairs of cards you confuse with each other, the most frequent first.
tools.get_progress: A snapshot of your learning: totals, recent reviews, due counts and what you study now.
tools.get_study_stats: Study statistics: reviews per day, active days and study minutes.
tools.get_cefr_level: Your current CEFR level and the language you study now.
tools.get_assessment_results: Your placement test results per language and level.
tools.get_course_progress: Your place in the course: progress per CEFR level, the next lesson and recent lessons with scores.
tools.get_lesson_content: The teaching content of a course lesson: grammar, dialogue, vocabulary and recap.
tools.get_reading_progress: The books you read in the app library, with the chapter and paragraph you reached.
tools.list_workspace_entries: Your notebook entries, newest first. Up to 30.
tools.get_workspace_attempts: Your answered exercises: your answer, the expected answer and whether it was correct. Up to 50.
tools.update_workspace_entry: Changes the title, text or notes of a notebook entry.
tools.delete_workspace_entry: Deletes a notebook entry on all your devices. This cannot be undone.
tools.search_media_decks: Searches the Zenzu library of ready-made word decks for films and TV series.
tools.get_media_deck: The cards of one film or one episode. Up to 60.

mcpPage.promptsIntro: Prompts are ready-made tasks that use the tools above. Your client can offer them as commands.

prompts.vocab_from_text: Picks the most useful words from a text you give and saves them as cards in one batch. Arguments: text (required), deck (optional). Saving needs “Allow writes”.
prompts.review_session: Quizzes you on your due cards one at a time and records each answer. Argument: language (optional). Recording needs “Allow writes”.
prompts.weekly_report: Builds a weekly report: activity, trouble words, your place in the course and one focus for next week.

rules: Every request needs a personal token in the header Authorization: Bearer zmcp_…. You create the token in the app under Settings → AI agents.

A token can only read, unless you tick “Allow writes” when you create it. Writing lets the assistant create, edit and delete decks and cards, move cards, record reviews and write notebooks. Deleting a deck also deletes its cards and cannot be undone.
When you create a token, you choose when it expires: in 30 days, in 90 days, in a year or never. The default is 90 days. An expired token stops working.
You can have up to 10 active tokens and create up to 20 tokens a day.
Revoke a token at any time in the app. It stops working at once.

Rate limits: 60 requests a minute and 1,000 an hour for each token, and 120 a minute and 2,000 an hour for your account over all its tokens. Above a limit, the server answers with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header.
Daily limits for your account, per UTC day: 3,000 recorded reviews and 2,000 write units. A new card or deck costs one unit. Notebook text costs one unit for each started 10 KB that is saved.
Each request carries one JSON-RPC message of up to 256 KB. Batches are refused.
An assistant sees only your account. It cannot reach other people’s data.

faq.q: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a: No. Zenzu hosts the server. Your assistant connects to its URL over HTTP.
Claude, Cursor or another assistant, if it can connect to a remote MCP server over HTTP and send your token in the Authorization header.

faq.q: Can the assistant change or delete my data?
faq.a: Only with a token that has “Allow writes”. The server refuses every write tool for a read-only token. With writes, the assistant can edit and delete. The delete tools tell the assistant to confirm with you first, but the server does not check that you agreed.

faq.q: Does a review in the chat count like a review in the app?
faq.a: Yes. review_card runs the same FSRS-6 scheduler as the app and updates the card’s schedule and your review log.

faq.q: Which MCP versions does the server support?
faq.a: Protocol versions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. The server only answers requests: it does not open a stream to send messages on its own.

items.a: Zenzu is a language learning app for learning from real content. You import YouTube videos, podcasts, articles or photos of text, tap any word or phrase to save it as a flashcard with its original sentence and native pronunciation, and review it with FSRS-6 spaced repetition. Lisa, the built-in AI coach, explains words and plans your study in your own language.

items.q: Which languages can I learn with Zenzu?
items.a: English, German, French and Spanish. Portuguese is coming soon. The app interface and the AI coach work in English, Ukrainian, German, French, Spanish and Portuguese.

items.q: Which devices does Zenzu run on?
items.a: iPhone and iPad with iOS 15 or later, Android phones and tablets through Google Play, and any modern web browser at app.zenzu.app.
Yes. Zenzu for Android is available on Google Play.

items.q: How is Zenzu different from Anki?
items.a: Both use FSRS spaced repetition, but in Anki you build cards yourself. Zenzu builds them from the content you are already watching, listening to or reading: every card keeps the sentence it came from and comes with native audio, so vocabulary is always learned in context.

items.q: Do I need to know English to use Zenzu?
items.a: No. You can use Zenzu entirely in Ukrainian, German, French, Spanish or Portuguese, so explanations, translations and coaching arrive in the language you think in.

items.q: What spaced repetition algorithm does Zenzu use?
items.a: FSRS-6, a modern open-source scheduler trained on large amounts of real review data. It predicts when you are about to forget each card and schedules the review right before that moment.
